linkedin.hook: Formal verification and isolated execution are shifting credit architecture on Soroban.
linkedin.copy:
Formal verification on Soroban changes the risk equation for composable leverage. Blend v2 standardizes debt accounting via b-tokens, establishing audited base assets that maintain verifiable reserves. On testnet, Vanna integrates these tokens inside isolated SmartAccounts rather than routing leverage through shared liquidity pools.

Architecture dictates liquidation safety. With Mercury indexer streaming state transitions at ~320ms latency and base network fees anchored at 0.00014 XLM, our risk engine monitors account solvency deterministically. Operators can maintain a 1.10x Health Factor floor during continuous compounding loops without exposing the clearinghouse to bad debt cascades.

Credit primitives should be evaluated on execution certainty rather than theoretical yields. We are moving away from monolithic shared-pool risk models toward auditable, containerized leverage accounts on Stellar. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

reddit.hook: Technical breakdown: Integrating Blend v2 b-tokens into Soroban SmartAccounts for composable leverage
reddit.copy:
Blend v2 b-tokens solve a specific problem on Soroban: they package debt and supply positions into verifiable, transferable tokens that other contracts can inspect deterministically. Over the past few weeks, we built the testnet credit layer for Vanna to consume these primitives directly inside isolated SmartAccount proxies.

The architecture centers on composable leverage without pooled counterparty liability. Most lending aggregators lump user collateral into a shared contract, exposing every user to systemic contagion if an oracle delays an update or a bad debt auction fails. We took an isolated approach. Each user deploys a SmartAccount contract that holds their collateral and interacts with Blend pools.

From an operational standpoint, this keeps execution clean. State changes register through the Mercury indexer within ~320ms. SmartAccount execution fees remain locked at 0.00014 XLM fixed gas per interaction. The risk engine enforces a 1.10x Health Factor floor, liquidating via localized auctions only within the individual undercollateralized account.

Because b-tokens reflect both principal and accrued interest, a SmartAccount can mint bUSDC, borrow XLM against it, swap back to USDC, and re-deposit into the pool in a single atomic transaction bundle. You capture the spread on testnet with deterministic state guarantees.

To test the pipeline yourself, connect your Soroban wallet on testnet, mint test assets, and deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance

Disclosure: I am an engineer at Vanna Protocol building composable credit primitives on Stellar. Feedback on execution traces and risk parameters is appreciated.
